title: pennsylvania-lpm Policy Brief Manifest
description: The compilation unit: which policy-principle records go into one audience-tailored brief, in what order, with what framing. Identical purpose to deutsche_lp's policy-brief-manifest.schema.json -- a manifest is the input a future compiler would take, and today serves as an explicit, checkable record of 'this is what we'd tell audience X, built from exactly these grounded principles.'

audience.description: Who this brief is written for. Same vocabulary as nys_lp's policy-brief-manifest.schema.json (itself adapted from deutsche_lp for the US institutional landscape) -- 'nonprofit-network-partner' covers an advocacy/grassroots organization like Pennsylvania Citizens for Science as readily as a curriculum nonprofit; 'policy-actor' covers a state legislator's office or a State Board of Education member.

audienceDetail.description: Free-text specifics, e.g. 'Pennsylvania State Board of Education members ahead of a standards-adoption vote' rather than just 'state-education-official'.

purpose.description: What this brief is trying to accomplish with this audience -- one or two sentences.

principleIds.description: Ordered list of policy-principle ids this brief compiles. Order matters -- it's the brief's own argument order.

framingNotes.description: Tone/emphasis guidance for whoever (human or LLM) drafts the actual brief text from these principles.

status.description: Manifest lifecycle -- distinct from whether an actual brief document has been written yet.
